summary:
The Earth Information Jukebox – Listen to How Earth Changes

We developed The Earth Information Jukebox, a technological project that transforms NASA’s scientific data about our planet into accessible sensory experiences.

Our goal is to help people with visual and hearing disabilities understand Earth’s changes. For blind and visually impaired people, we propose sounds, voice commands, and a voice reader to make information accessible. For deaf and hard-of-hearing people, we incorporate colors, animations, and light signals to represent environmental changes.

This project addresses the challenge of making science more accessible through different senses. It is important because it promotes inclusion and demonstrates that everyone deserves access to scientific knowledge.
details: The Earth Information Jukebox turns real NASA Earth data into music so people can hear how the planet is changing. Its seven tracks cover global temperature, Arctic sea ice, ocean heat, CO₂, night lights, lightning, and possible climate futures based on IPCC projections. Each data point becomes a sound: a warmer year plays a higher note, and more ice adds more bells. The main benefit is accessibility, because blind and low-vision people can explore data that is usually shared only as images. Everything can be used without a screen, through voice guidance, spoken commands, the keyboard, and a game controller that vibrates with the data. We want to make climate science more inclusive and more memorable. We built it with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Tone.js, the Web Audio API, Three.js, the Web Speech API, and the Gamepad API, plus PowerShell scripts to process the data, and the images come from NASA’s Scientific Visualization Studio. It’s creative because it treats data as real music without changing what the data says. As a team, we focused on scientific accuracy, keeping the information clear even through a single speaker, and making it run in any browser without installing anything..
